quizzes.title: Olympus & Beyond
quizzes.description: Gods, monsters and heroes from Greek and Roman myth.

questions.q: Who is the king of the gods in Greek mythology?
questions.note: He ruled from Mount Olympus and hurled thunderbolts.

questions.q: In Roman mythology, Mars is the god of war.
questions.note: His Greek equivalent is Ares, and the month of March is named after him.

questions.q: In Greek myth, what was the Gorgon Medusa's hair made of?
questions.note: Anyone who looked directly at her was turned to stone.

questions.q: Which Greek hero could only be wounded in his heel?
questions.note: His mother Thetis dipped him in the River Styx, holding him by the heel.

questions.q: Which Greek god of the sea carries a trident?
questions.note: His Roman counterpart is Neptune.

questions.q: Who opened a jar, often called a box, that released evils into the world?
questions.note: Only hope remained inside when the lid was closed.

questions.q: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of wisdom.
questions.note: Athena is the goddess of wisdom; Aphrodite is the goddess of love and beauty.

questions.q: The Roman god Cupid is equivalent to which Greek god?
questions.note: His arrows made gods and mortals fall in love.

questions.q: Which hero of Greek myth performed the Twelve Labours?
questions.note: Hercules is the Roman form of his name; accept either.

questions.q: What hollow wooden figure did the Greeks use to get inside the city of Troy?
questions.note: The trick is credited to the cunning hero Odysseus.

quizzes.title: Tales from Asgard
quizzes.description: Hammers, wolves and world trees from Norse mythology.

questions.q: What is the name of Thor's hammer?
questions.note: It was forged by dwarves; Gungnir is Odin's spear.

questions.q: Odin gave up one of his eyes to drink from Mimir's well.
questions.note: The water of the well granted him great wisdom.

questions.q: What is the name of the great world tree in Norse mythology?
questions.note: Its branches and roots connect the nine worlds.

questions.q: Which Norse trickster god is the father of the giant wolf Fenrir?
questions.note: His other children include the world serpent Jörmungandr and Hel.

questions.q: What is the name of the rainbow bridge that leads to Asgard?
questions.note: It connects Asgard with Midgard, the world of humans.

questions.q: What is the name of the doom of the gods, the final battle in Norse myth?
questions.note: In the battle, Odin is swallowed by the wolf Fenrir.

questions.q: The goddess Freyja rides in a chariot pulled by two goats.
questions.note: Freyja's chariot is drawn by cats; it is Thor's chariot that goats pull.

questions.q: Odin's ravens Huginn and Muninn stand for what?
questions.note: They fly across the world each day and report back to Odin.

questions.q: Which Norse god lost his hand in the jaws of the wolf Fenrir?
questions.note: Also spelled Týr; Tuesday is named after him.

questions.q: Which Norse god is the ever-watchful guardian of the rainbow bridge?
questions.note: He will blow the horn Gjallarhorn to announce Ragnarök.

quizzes.title: Gods of the Nile
quizzes.description: Sun gods, jackals and the journey to the afterlife in ancient Egypt.

questions.q: Which Egyptian god is usually shown with the head of a jackal?
questions.note: He watched over mummification and guarded the dead.

questions.q: Who was the ancient Egyptian sun god, said to sail across the sky in a boat each day?
questions.note: Also spelled Re; he was often merged with Amun as Amun-Ra.

questions.q: Which Egyptian god was killed by his brother Set and became ruler of the underworld?
questions.note: His wife Isis gathered his scattered body and restored him.

questions.q: The Egyptian god Sobek was shown with the head of a hippopotamus.
questions.note: Sobek had a crocodile's head; Taweret was the hippo goddess.

questions.q: In Egyptian myth, the god Horus is the son of which goddess?
questions.note: Horus avenged his father Osiris by battling Set.

questions.q: Which Egyptian goddess was usually shown as a cat or a cat-headed woman?
questions.note: Her cult centre was the city of Bubastis in the Nile Delta.

questions.q: In Egyptian belief, a dead person's heart was weighed against the feather of Maat.
questions.note: A heart heavier than the feather was devoured by the monster Ammit.

questions.q: Which sky goddess was said to swallow the sun each evening and give birth to it each morning?
questions.note: Her star-covered body arches over her brother Geb, the earth god.

questions.q: Which ibis-headed Egyptian god was the god of writing and wisdom?
questions.note: He was said to have invented hieroglyphic writing.

questions.q: In ancient Egypt, the scarab beetle was a symbol of what?
questions.note: The god Khepri was pictured as a scarab rolling the sun across the sky.

quizzes.title: Epics of India
quizzes.description: Heroes, battles and exiles from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.

questions.q: Who is traditionally credited with composing the Sanskrit Ramayana?
questions.note: He is honoured as the Adi Kavi, the first poet.

questions.q: The Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata.
questions.note: It has 700 verses and is set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.

questions.q: Who was the eldest of King Dhritarashtra's hundred sons in the Mahabharata?
questions.note: His rivalry with the Pandavas led to the Kurukshetra war.

questions.q: Which demon king of Lanka abducted Sita in the Ramayana?
questions.note: He is usually depicted with ten heads.

questions.q: Who was the mother of the Pandavas Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna?
questions.note: Madri was the mother of the twins Nakula and Sahadeva.

questions.q: In the Ramayana, which vulture king was mortally wounded trying to stop Ravana?
questions.note: Before dying, he told Rama which way Ravana had taken Sita.

questions.q: The Kauravas won the Kurukshetra war in the Mahabharata.
questions.note: The Pandavas won the 18-day war.

questions.q: Which of Rama's brothers went with him into exile in the forest?
questions.note: Bharata ruled in Rama's name, placing Rama's sandals on the throne.

questions.q: To which Pandava warrior did Krishna deliver the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita?
questions.note: Krishna served as his charioteer during the war.

questions.q: Which city was Rama's capital in the Ramayana?
questions.note: Ayodhya stands on the banks of the Sarayu river in northern India.
